Merge spells that follow each other or overlap into one

Source: R/merge_spells.R
merge_spells.Rd

A stay in hospital moved between wards, a job continued with a new contract, an address re-registered the day after: registers often record one spell as several, back to back or overlapping, and every count of spells, lengths and transitions is wrong until they are merged. describe_spells() shows how often it happens; merge_spells() does the merging, one row per merged spell.

Usage

merge_spells(data, id, start, end, by = NULL, max_gap = 0)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble with one row per spell.

id

Column(s) identifying the unit (tidy-select), e.g. cpr.

start, end

Columns with the first and last day (or period) of each spell. A missing end means an ongoing spell.

by

Optional column(s) (tidy-select) that must be equal for spells to be merged, e.g. employer.

max_gap

Largest number of days (or periods) between two spells that are still merged: 0 merges spells that follow the next day, -1 only spells that share a day. A whole number from -1.

Value

A tibble (a data.table if data is one) with the id and by columns, start, end and n_spells, one row per merged spell. Units come in the order they first appear in data, and each unit's spells by start; use dplyr::arrange() to sort by the id columns.

Details

When spells are merged

Within a unit, spells are taken in order of start, and a spell is merged into the one before when the number of days between them, from the latest end so far to its start, is at most max_gap:

  • max_gap = 0 (default) merges spells that overlap, share a day, or where one starts the day after the other ends: the transfers.

  • max_gap = -1 merges only spells that share at least one day, and keeps transfers apart.

  • max_gap = 30 also merges spells less than a month apart, e.g. a readmission within 30 days counted as the same episode.

The merged spell runs from the first start to the latest end, and is ongoing (missing end) if any of its spells is. Use by to merge only spells that agree in a column, e.g. the employer or the status, so a job followed directly by unemployment stays two spells: spells are then grouped by the id and by columns together.

Columns other than id, by, start and end are dropped, as one merged spell may have several values for them; n_spells counts the spells merged into each row. Rows with a missing start or an end before the start are dropped with a message, as in spells_to_panel().

start and end may be dates or whole numbers (years, month numbers), compared by that unit.

Why it is fast

It shares the compiled pass of describe_spells(): units are compressed to integer ids (see checkpoints), spells are sorted once by data.table's radix sort, and one sequential pass relates each spell to the earlier ones. The result is not sorted by the id columns, which on a population register means sorting millions of strings and would take most of the time; units keep the order of the data, which for an extract sorted by cpr is the same.

See also

describe_spells() to see how many spells follow each other or overlap, ensure_no_overlap() to require that none overlap.

Examples

admissions <- data.frame(
  cpr   = c("a", "a", "a", "b", "b"),
  start = as.Date(c("2020-01-01", "2020-01-11", "2020-03-01",
                    "2020-01-01", "2020-01-05")),
  end   = as.Date(c("2020-01-10", "2020-01-20", "2020-03-05",
                    "2020-01-31", "2020-01-10")),
  ward  = c("A", "B", "A", "A", "C")
)
# a is moved from ward A to B on 11 January: one stay, then a new one
merge_spells(admissions, cpr, start, end)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>   cpr   start      end        n_spells
#>   <chr> <date>     <date>        <int>
#> 1 a     2020-01-01 2020-01-20        2
#> 2 a     2020-03-01 2020-03-05        1
#> 3 b     2020-01-01 2020-01-31        2

# Readmissions within 60 days count as the same episode
merge_spells(admissions, cpr, start, end, max_gap = 60)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   cpr   start      end        n_spells
#>   <chr> <date>     <date>        <int>
#> 1 a     2020-01-01 2020-03-05        3
#> 2 b     2020-01-01 2020-01-31        2

# Only stays in the same ward
merge_spells(admissions, cpr, start, end, by = ward)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 5
#>   cpr   ward  start      end        n_spells
#>   <chr> <chr> <date>     <date>        <int>
#> 1 a     A     2020-01-01 2020-01-10        1
#> 2 a     A     2020-03-01 2020-03-05        1
#> 3 a     B     2020-01-11 2020-01-20        1
#> 4 b     A     2020-01-01 2020-01-31        1
#> 5 b     C     2020-01-05 2020-01-10        1
